payload.source_label: Equation (1.1): q_t + A q_x = 0 for a constant real m by m matrix A

contract.statement: In one spatial dimension, the homogeneous first-order constant-coefficient linear system for an unknown real m-component field q(x,t), with q : R × R → R^m and a constant real m × m matrix A, is written q_t(x,t) + A q_x(x,t) = 0. Subscripts mean partial derivatives in time and space. This introduces the equation to be satisfied; it neither asserts that arbitrary q satisfies it nor supplies an existence or uniqueness theorem. The displayed derivative notation suggests a classical pointwise reading, but regularity and explicit quantifier scope are not specified. Additional properties of A are needed for hyperbolicity. [Raw PDF page 23, printed Chapter 1 page 1, equation (1.1) and its enclosing paragraph.]
assumptions: The class being described consists of homogeneous first-order systems in one spatial dimension, in the constant-coefficient linear case. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, sentence spanning equation (1.1).]
The coefficient matrix is constant, real, square, and compatible with the m-component state. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, description of A following (1.1).]

The display is naturally read as an equation in the independent variables, rather than an equality at one distinguished point; the source does not write an explicit universal quantifier over x and t. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, equation (1.1) and q : R × R → R^m.]

A classical pointwise reading requires the displayed partial derivatives to exist where the equation is asserted. This is an analyst inference from derivative notation; the selected passage does not prescribe a differentiability class. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, equation (1.1) and explicit partial-derivative convention.]

No initial data, boundary data, or restricted time interval are attached to the selected equation. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, complete paragraph introducing (1.1), including the stated domain R × R.]

Additional matrix properties are needed to call the general system hyperbolic; those properties are deferred and are not hypotheses of the equation-form description itself. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, hyperbolicity qualification following the description of A.]
quantifiers: m is the finite component count used in R^m and in the dimensions m × m of A; the passage does not provide an explicit quantified range for m. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, descriptions of q and A following (1.1).]
q : R × R → R^m is the vector of unknown functions. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, explicit type of q following (1.1).]
A is a constant m × m matrix with real entries. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, description of A following (1.1).]

x is the single real spatial variable and t is the real time variable, in the argument order q(x,t). [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, time-dependent and one-space-dimension context, displayed (1.1), and domain of q.]
